model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for six different model configurations, with the x-axis representing the number of iterations (#Iteration) ranging from 0 to 140,000 in increments of 20,000, and the y-axis representing Loss, scaled from 2.4 to 3.4 in increments of 0.1. The “Vanilla” model (purple line) starts at approximately 3.4 loss and steadily decreases to around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” model (blue line) begins near 3.4, drops sharply to about 2.7 by 20,000 iterations, then gradually declines to ~2.62 by 140,000. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange line) starts slightly below 3.4, falls to ~2.65 by 20,000, and continues to ~2.54 by 140,000. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green line) follows a similar trajectory to the orange line, ending slightly higher at ~2.56. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red line) begins near 3.4, drops to ~2.68 by 20,000, and stabilizes near 2.53 by 140,000. Finally, “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue line) starts at ~3.4, declines rapidly to ~2.7 by 20,000, then slowly decreases to ~2.6 by 140,000, remaining consistently higher than the other SepLLM variants after ~40,000 iterations. All lines exhibit a steep initial drop followed by a slower convergence, with some models showing minor fluctuations or noise in later iterations.
